newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Shell Brasil buys Brazil natgas company.
newsitem.headline: Shell Brasil buys Brazil natgas company.

text.p: Shell Brasil SA, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell, bought private Brazilian natgas company Petrogas for an undisclosed sum in a bid to strengthen its position in Brazil's promising natural gas market, a senior company official said.
"The natural gas market in Brazil is relatively small," the official said. "It has a lot of potential and is bound to grow over the next few years."

He said that currently natgas accounted for only two percent of Brazilian energy consumption, but the government was promoting gas as a source of energy and wanted it to account for 10 percent of consumption by 2005. In the industrialized world gas provides 25 percent of energy consumption on average, he said.

Petrogas, in Campinas, Sao Paulo state, has a four-percent share of the liquified petroleum gas market, three filling plants plus a 50 percent share in a fourth filling plant, 800 workers and 2,000 clients.
The price paid for Petrogas could not be disclosed due to a confidentiality clause in the contract.

It is Shell's second purchase in the Brazilian natural gas sector in recent weeks. In January, Shell Brasil paid 74 million reais ($71.2 million) for a 20-percent stake in Sao Paulo state-owned Comgas, which is due to be privatized in October.
The official said Shell was studying the possibility of increasing its Comgas stake when the company is privatized. The firm accounts for 30 percent of all natural gas sold in Brazil.

At the time of the Comgas acquisition, Shell Brasil President Willem Goebel said Shell would seek to become Brazil's second largest natgas distributor once the government approves a new law regulating the opening of the country's oil sector.
((Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
